fix(money): use ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212

round_money documented banker's rounding but was quantizing with
ROUND_HALF_UP, breaking tests/test_money.py in the nightly build.
Switch to ROUND_HALF_EVEN.

args.head: fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: fix(money): use ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` was quantizing with `ROUND_HALF_UP` despite its docstring claiming banker's rounding.

## Changes
- `src/money.py`: switch rounding mode from `ROUND_HALF_UP` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` to match the documented behavior and FIN-212.

## Testing
- CI run on this branch (`ci-0001`) passed, which was the failing case in the nightly build (e.g. `round_money(Decimal("2.665")) == Decimal("2.66")`).

## Purpose
Fix the failing nightly build so the fix ships in today's release.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

- **Root cause:** `src/money.py` documented banker's rounding (FIN-212) in its docstring but actually used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, which broke `tests/test_money.py` (e.g. `2.665` rounding up to `2.67` instead of down to `2.66`) in the nightly build.
- **Fix:** Created branch `fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding` and committed a one-line change switching the quantize rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.
- **CI:** Triggered run `ci-0001` on the branch — it passed.
- **PR:** Opened PR #101 against main (`https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101`), requested code-owner review, and per policy obtained code-owner approval via `ask_human` before merging.
- **Merged:** PR #101 is merged into main, so the fix will ship in today's release.
